setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Git responds with a version number

setupSteps.title: Install Node LTS
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Node responds with a version number

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.verifierLabel: Terminal is open

steps.title: Check Git and Node
steps.verifierLabel: Git works and Node is a supported version

steps.title: Copy NitroAI to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d NitroAI/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/NitroAI.git
fi
steps.verifierLabel: The NitroAI folder exists

steps.title: Open the NitroAI folder
steps.verifierLabel: Your terminal prompt is inside the NitroAI folder

steps.title: Use the reviewed version
steps.verifierLabel: Git reports the reviewed commit

expect.prompt: Has git finished checking out the commit — does the terminal show a line beginning "HEAD is now at", with the prompt back and ready?

hints: If git says a pathspec did not match, you are not inside the NitroAI folder yet — run cd NitroAI first.
"You are in 'detached HEAD' state" is expected here, not an error.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.verifierLabel: The command finishes without an error

expect.prompt: Has npm finished installing — does the terminal show a summary such as "added N packages" and a fresh prompt, with no error?

hints: If it stops on the Node version, install Node 20.19+ or 22 LTS (not 21.x) and run it again.
A permission error usually means the folder was cloned somewhere you cannot write — clone it under your home folder.

steps.title: Build the app
steps.verifierLabel: A NitroAI .dmg appears in release

steps.title: Put NitroAI in Applications
steps.body: Copy the freshly built app into Applications so it's a real, launchable Mac app.
steps.command:
if [ "$(uname -m)" = "arm64" ]; then
ditto release/mac-arm64/NitroAI.app /Applications/NitroAI.app
else
ditto release/mac/NitroAI.app /Applications/NitroAI.app
fi
steps.verifierLabel: NitroAI.app is in your Applications folder

steps.title: Open NitroAI
steps.body: Built on your own machine, so macOS opens it without any warning.
steps.verifierLabel: NitroAI opens

steps.title: Choose local or cloud AI
steps.body: Use Ollama locally, or add a provider key. Ollama downloads on first use.
steps.verifierLabel: NitroAI finishes its first-run setup

steps.title: Try one real task
steps.body: Turn a real lecture, PDF, or video into notes, flashcards, and a quiz.
steps.verifierLabel: Generated notes appear in the installed app
